q: On highway patrol you find a dhaba owner barring Dalit truck drivers from the common well and tables, claiming it is private property and custom.
options: Advise compromise as it is a private dhaba and ask drivers to use another hotel
Register case for enforcing disability from wells/shops and ensure access with protection
Take both sides to panchayat for settlement and record a CSR only
File a civil suit on behalf of drivers and wait for court order
expl: Bar on access to shops, wells, tanks applies against private owners too.
why: The ban on denial of access to public shops and sources of water binds private persons, not only the State. On road the SI must treat refusal as offence, register FIR and ensure entry.
trapnote: Trap: private property claim does not defeat equality of access.

q: A Dalit labourer reports public humiliation and beating for using the village path. The writer refuses FIR, saying first get DSP opinion as it looks like a civil dispute.
options: Hold FIR till preliminary enquiry and DSP opinion are completed
Register FIR immediately and forward for investigation, enquiry can follow
Record GD entry only and advise complaint to revenue court
Insist on compromise since both sides are from same village
expl: Atrocity law mandates immediate registration on disclosed offence.
why: Registration of disclosed atrocity offence is mandatory to protect equality and dignity. In station duty the SI must register first and let investigation test truth.
trapnote: Trap: enquiry-before-FIR plea to delay atrocity registration.

q: During constable verification drive the SHO orders 80% posts reserved for his mandal youth to please local leaders, rejecting outsiders despite merit.
options: Follow order as domicile preference ensures local policing advantage
Apply only constitutionally permitted reservation for backward classes with merit, reject 100% local quota
Reject all reservation and select purely on physical marks
Keep selection pending till leaders approve final list
expl: Equality permits protective reservation but forbids wholesale exclusion.
why: Equal opportunity in public employment allows reasonable classification for backward classes, not blanket local monopoly. On board duty the SI must record objection and apply roster correctly.
trapnote: Trap: confuses lawful reservation with political local quota.

q: At temple bandobast the priest blocks Dalit women from the temple tank citing age-old custom, and the crowd supports him.
options: Respect custom to avoid breach of peace and divert them to another tank
Enforce entry, remove obstruction and bind over obstructors to maintain order
Close temple temporarily and refer matter to endowment tribunal
Allow entry only on non-festival days as middle path
expl: Untouchability is abolished and custom cannot justify denial.
why: Abolition of untouchability makes disability enforcement an offence and custom void. On bandobast the SI must guarantee access and prevent breach by obstructors, not victims.
trapnote: Trap: custom and peace plea used to deny temple entry.

q: For women and tribal constable candidates the recruitment notification gives relaxed height and chest norms. A rejected general candidate alleges discrimination at your helpdesk.
options: Cancel relaxation and apply single uniform standard to all
Uphold relaxation as reasonable classification with clear nexus to recruitment goal
Disqualify all relaxed candidates pending court clarification
Refer candidate to file writ and stop recruitment
expl: Equals treated alike, unequals may differ if differentia is intelligible and linked.
why: Equality forbids arbitrary action but permits reasonable classification with intelligible differentia and rational nexus. At helpdesk the SI must explain validity and continue lawful recruitment.
trapnote: Trap: treats any difference as illegal discrimination.
